practice: A compound contains 40% C, 6.67% H and 53.33% O and has molecular mass 180. Determine its empirical and molecular formula.
0.2 g of an organic compound on combustion gives 0.44 g CO₂ and 0.18 g H₂O. Find its empirical formula.
An oxide of nitrogen contains 30.4% nitrogen and has vapour density 46. Find its molecular formula.
A hydrated salt contains 36.1% water of crystallisation and its anhydrous salt has molar mass 120 g mol⁻¹. Find the number of water molecules per formula unit.
Explain why an empirical formula alone cannot identify a compound, with a suitable example.
